content: The apparatus behind every page: dates, terms, sources, and the record of what has been corrected.
Everything on this website that is not argument is here: the tools a reader needs to check the argument, and the record of how the argument has been tested.

The timeline sets every gospel, letter, council and manuscript on one line from the birth of Jesus to the Qur’an, so that the distance between an event and its earliest record can be seen at a glance. The glossary defines the Arabic, Greek, Hebrew and Syriac terms and the vocabulary of New Testament scholarship that the articles use without stopping to explain. The source library indexes every work cited, by kind, with the pages that lean on it.

The second half is the website answering for itself. The FAQs give the questions people search for most, each answered in under 60 words and linked to the page with the evidence. Objections and replies states the strongest Christian objections to this website’s case, in the form a Christian apologist would accept, and answers each. Responses to named articles does the same for 4 published articles and one website, claim by claim.
The corrections log records every error found on the website, with what the page said and what it now says, so that a reader can see the website has been wrong and how it put the matter right.

Read the articles with the glossary and the timeline open; every date and term in them is here. Where an article’s source list names a work, the source library gives its edition and the other pages that use it. If you think an article is wrong, the contact page says how to report it and what a useful report contains. A Christian reader with a reply will find the best replies published and answered on the objections and responses pages, and a good one will end up there.

<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>Where can I check the sources used on this website?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->

Every article lists its sources at the foot, and the source library indexes all of them by kind, from the Qur’an and the Greek New Testament to the commentaries, the church fathers, the critical scholarship and the manuscripts, with the pages that lean on each.
<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>Is there a timeline of the gospels and the Qur’an?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->

Yes. The timeline runs from the birth of Jesus to the Qur’an and beyond, with every gospel, letter, council and manuscript dated, so the distance between an event and its earliest record can be seen at a glance.
<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>How do I report an error on this website?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->

Through the contact page, giving the page, the sentence and the source that shows it is wrong. A report that is right is corrected on the page and recorded in the corrections log with what the page said and what it now says.
<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>Has this website ever been wrong?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->
Yes, and the corrections log says where: scanning errors in the printed gospel text, 2 broken links, and a count of Thomas sayings that was revised. The log is kept newest first and never pruned.
<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>Where are Christian objections answered?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->

On Objections and replies, which states each objection in the form a Christian apologist would accept and answers it, and on Responses to named articles, which answers 4 published articles and one website claim by claim. The FAQs give the short answers.
<details class="wp-block-details is-style-faq"><summary>What do Injīl, taḥrīf and muhaymin mean?</summary><!-- wp:paragraph -->

Injīl is the Qur’an’s word for the revelation given to Jesus. Taḥrīf is alteration, of meaning or of text. Muhaymin, “guardian”, is what the Qur’an calls itself over the earlier scripture (5:48), and gives this website its measure. These and 60 other terms are in the glossary.
The study began with a question and ends with its answers. The FAQs give the short ones; The Islamic Dilemma, answered gives the whole case in one page, and is the place to start again.
